title: Foundation controls and processes: access, change, data, procurement & travel
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:
This playbook collects Redwood Inference’s baseline, cross-functional controls and step-by-step processes for: access & permissions, change management, data lifecycle, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel, and commonly used internal templates. It is intended as the canonical operational reference for engineering, product, people-ops, and finance teams.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems or customer data.
- Operational exceptions (e.g., security incident response) are handled by the Security incident process; see related pages.
- Owners listed below are accountable for maintaining each section and ensuring team-level procedures map to these standards.

Key principles:
- Least privilege: grant the minimum permissions required and use temporary elevated access where practical.
- Segregation of duties: approvals should not be self-authorized for procurement, vendor onboarding, or high-risk changes.
- Auditability: every approval and change must be traceable in systems that retain logs for the retention period defined in Data Management.
- Cost-awareness: procurement and expense approvals must reference budget lines and expected ROI.

Definitions (short):
- Admin group: role-based group with elevated configuration privileges (e.g., network-admin, infra-admin).
- High-risk change: any change that may impact production latency, security posture, or customer data availability.
- Sensitive data: PII, customer secrets, or regulated data subject to additional controls described below.

Access & permissions:
Owner: Security (operational policies maintained jointly with People Ops)
Purpose: Centralize how access is requested, approved, and revoked to reduce blast radius and support audits.

Standard process for granting access:
1) Request: employee or contractor opens an access request via the Access Portal (internal URL: /access-portal) and identifies the resource, justification, and duration (if temporary).
2) Manager approval: direct manager must approve role justification and provide a business justification in the request.
3) Owner approval: resource owner (service or team owner) must sign off for production and sensitive resources.
4) Security review: for requests involving customer data or elevated privileges, Security performs a risk review (within 48 hours).
5) Provision: IAM system (OKTA + internal RBAC) provisions access; request and approval chain are recorded.
6) Scheduled review: access with duration > 90 days is automatically included in quarterly access reviews.

Revocation and emergency access:
- Revocation should be initiated by manager or security via the Access Portal. Offboarding triggers automatic deprovisioning: accounts, keys, VPN tokens, and cloud roles are revoked within 2 hours of HR offboard confirmation.
- Emergency access: just-in-time (JIT) admin elevations are provided via the Privileged Access system and expire within the session window (default 4 hours). All JIT sessions are logged in SIEM and reviewed weekly.

Change management:
Owner: Eng Platform / Eng SRE (policy maintained with Product)
Purpose: Ensure predictable, auditable changes to systems and services while minimizing customer impact.

Change classification table:
| Type | Examples | Approval required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard (low-risk) | routine configuration updates, non-prod infra patching | Auto-approved via change queue; notify SRE team |
| Normal (moderate-risk) | model rollout, database schema migration | Manager + service owner approval; change ticket in CHG system |
| High-risk / Emergency | production DB rollback, broad network change | SRE on-call + Eng Platform lead approval; Emergency CAB post-facto review |

Pre-deployment checklist (Normal + High-risk):
- Impact analysis documented on the change ticket
- Backout plan and validation steps included
- SLA/RPO/RTO implications enumerated
- Load, canary, and smoke test schedules defined
- Communication plan with customer-facing teams (Support, CS)

Change windows and Canary policy:
- Normal changes should target low-traffic windows or use progressive rollout (canaries at 1%, 10%, 50%).
- Canary metrics: error rate, tail latency (p99), token drop rate for inference services. Canary fails when error rate or p99 latency increases by > 25% relative to baseline for 10m.

Post-change reviews and audits:
- All High-risk changes require a postmortem within 72 hours and a closure signoff from the change owner.
- Monthly change audit report is distributed to Eng leadership.

Data management and retention:
Owner: Security + Data Governance
Purpose: Define lifecycle for all company and customer data to meet compliance, privacy, and operational needs.

Data classification levels:
- Public: documentation intended for public consumption
- Internal: operational data not containing PII or secrets
- Sensitive: PII, model training data tied to customers, API secrets
- Regulated: data covered by contractual/regulatory controls (e.g., GDPR special categories, HIPAA)

Retention matrix (summary):
| Data type | Retention | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audit logs | 2 years (compressed) | Security |
| Billing & invoices | 7 years | Finance |
| Backups (non-sensitive) | 30 days rolling | Eng Infra |
| Customer model inputs (sensitive) | Configured per contract; default 30 days | Product / Legal |

Access to sensitive data:
- Must be approved via an elevated access workflow (see Access & permissions).
- Access requires MFA, device posture check, and mandatory data handling training.
- Sensitive exports are encrypted with customer-specific keys where required.

Data disposal:
- Secure wipe procedures for cloud storage and on-prem disks are documented in Eng Infra runbooks.
- Deletion requests (customer or internal) are processed within 30 days unless contractual restrictions apply.

Procurement & expenses:
Owner: Finance (procurement team)
Purpose: Ensure cost control, vendor compliance, and transparent approvals.

Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
1) Low-value purchases (< $5,000): budget owner approval via procurement system.
2) Mid-value purchases ($5,000 – $50,000): budget owner + Finance procurement lead approval.
3) High-value purchases (> $50,000): VP-level signoff + Legal review for contract terms.

Purchase request workflow:
1) Raise PR in Procurement Portal with cost center and business case
2) Procurement validates vendor and checks existing contracts or preferred suppliers
3) Finance budgets against runway/OKR allocations and approves/rejects within 3 business days
4) Purchase order (PO) issued and vendor notified

Expense policy highlights:
- Travel expenses are reimbursed per Travel Policy below; employees must submit within 30 days with receipts.
- Card usage: corporate cards must be reconciled weekly. Misuse or repeated exceptions will trigger review by Finance and People Ops.

Vendor management and onboarding:
Owner: Procurement + Legal
Purpose: Standardize vendor risk assessment, onboarding, contract lifecycle, and periodic review.

Vendor classification and controls:
- Category A (Strategic/High-risk): vendors handling customer data, infra providers, or critical software (renewal cadence, quarterly business reviews, SLA penalties).
- Category B (Business-support): SaaS tools without customer data, moderate risk (annual review).
- Category C (Low-cost / Consumable): office supplies, low-risk services (procurement-approved catalog).

Onboarding checklist (Category A):
1) Vendor risk assessment (security questionnaire + SOC2/ISO reports)
2) Legal contract negotiation with appropriate data processing addenda (DPA)
3) Finance sets payment terms and PO process
4) Procurement adds vendor to vendor registry and assigns owner
5) Quarterly health checks and SLA monitoring configured

Termination and offboarding:
- Contracted vendors must provide a data export and deletion plan. Procurement coordinates with Eng and Security to revoke access and rotate shared credentials.

Travel policy (concise):
Owner: People Ops + Finance
Purpose: Provide safe, cost-effective travel practices that balance employee comfort and budget discipline.

Key rules:
- Booking: employees should use the approved travel portal. Air travel in economy for trips < 6 hours; premium economy or business requires VP approval.
- Per diem: meal caps are country-specific and listed in the Travel Templates appendix.
- Approval: manager approval required for travel; trips > $5,000 require finance pre-approval.
- Safety: employees traveling to high-risk locations must register with People Ops and receive a brief safety checklist.

Templates and attachments:
- Expense form (example): attach receipts, indicate cost center, and tag attendees for team meals.
- Vendor risk questionnaire (condensed): security posture, certifications, encryption at rest, incident notification SLA.
- Change request template (CHG) with fields for backout plan and metrics to watch.
- Data export / deletion request template for customers.

(Templates are maintained in the central templates repository: /confluence/templates — link in related pages.)

Roles and responsibilities (summary):
- Finance: procurement governance, PO issuance, expense audits
- Legal: contract reviews, DPAs, vendor clauses
- Security: access policies, sensitive data controls, log retention
- Eng Platform / SRE: change approvals, production readiness checks, runbooks
- People Ops: travel safety, offboarding triggers, provisioning liaison

Monitoring and audit:
- Quarterly compliance reviews will validate adherence to the procurement matrix, access reviews, and change management records.
- Security and Finance run annual audits and publish a summary to leadership and the board.

Appendix — Quick references:
- Access request SLA: 48 hours for standard requests; 2 hours for offboarding deprovisioning
- Change canary fail thresholds: > 25% increase in error or p99 for 10m
- Procurement response times: 3 business days for mid-value requests

Revision history:
- 2026-11-15: Initial draft created by Maya Patel
- 2027-02-20: Consolidated reviewer feedback; updated procurement thresholds and access SLA

Contact and escalation:
- For policy clarifications, email ops-policies@redwood.ai or open a ticket in the internal Policy queue.
- Emergency security questions: security-oncall@redwood.ai (pager-enabled).
